name: Homemade Pita Bread
description: Soft, puffy pita breads that puff up beautifully in a hot oven

timing.notes: Includes 1 hour rise time and 10 minute rest periods

equipment.item: Heavy-duty baking sheet, cast iron pan, or ceramic baking tile
equipment.notes: Must be able to get very hot - preheated in oven
For keeping pitas warm and soft

equipment.alternative: Test water temperature by touch - should be warm, not hot

ingredients.notes: About 100-110°F - warm to touch, not hot
Freshly milled preferred but any whole wheat works
Unbleached preferred. Reserve 1/2 cup for kneading.

prep_steps.instruction: Set up your staging area: clear a large section of counter for kneading. Get out your large mixing bowl, measuring cups and spoons, and a clean kitchen towel.
prep_steps.notes: You'll need space for kneading and for 8 dough balls to rest

prep_steps.instruction: Measure 1 cup lukewarm water into the large mixing bowl. Water should feel warm but not hot - about bath temperature.
prep_steps.notes: Water that's too hot will kill the yeast; too cold won't activate it

prep_steps.instruction: Measure the yeast and sugar. Have them ready near the bowl.
Measure the whole wheat flour and 1/4 cup of the all-purpose flour into a small bowl for the sponge
prep_steps.notes: This makes the initial sponge mixture

prep_steps.instruction: Measure remaining 2 cups all-purpose flour into a medium bowl. Reserve 1/2 cup in a separate small bowl for kneading.
prep_steps.notes: Keep reserved flour handy for kneading and rolling

prep_steps.instruction: Measure olive oil and salt, keep near the main flour

cook_steps.instruction: Make the sponge: Add yeast and sugar to the lukewarm water in the large bowl. Stir to dissolve.

cues.visual: Yeast dissolves into water, mixture is cloudy

cook_steps.warnings: If yeast doesn't activate (foam) after 15 minutes, it's dead - start over with fresh yeast

cook_steps.instruction: Add the sponge flour (whole wheat + 1/4 cup AP flour) to the yeast water. Whisk to combine into a thin batter.

cues.visual: Smooth, thin batter with no dry lumps

cook_steps.instruction: Place bowl in a warm spot, uncovered. Let sit until frothy and bubbling.

cues.visual: Surface is covered with foam and bubbles, volume has increased
cues.audio: Tiny crackling sounds if you listen closely

cook_steps.warnings: Don't rush this - the sponge develops flavor

cook_steps.instruction: Add salt, olive oil, and nearly all of the main flour (reserve about 1/2 cup). Stir with wooden spoon until mixture forms a shaggy mass.

cues.visual: Ragged, shaggy dough - not smooth yet

cook_steps.warnings: Don't add all the flour - you need to adjust as you knead

cook_steps.instruction: Dust dough with a little reserved flour. Knead briefly in the bowl for 1 minute, incorporating any stray dry bits.

cues.visual: Dough starts to come together, still rough

cook_steps.instruction: Turn dough onto clean work surface. Knead lightly for 2 minutes until smooth. Cover with towel and let rest 10 minutes.

cues.visual: Dough is smooth and soft, slightly tacky but not sticky

cook_steps.warnings: Resist adding too much flour - dough should be soft and slightly moist

cook_steps.instruction: Knead again for 2 minutes. The dough should be smooth, soft, and pliable.

cues.visual: Smooth, elastic dough that springs back when poked

cook_steps.instruction: Clean the mixing bowl, return dough to it. Cover tightly with plastic wrap, then cover with towel. Place in warm spot to rise until doubled.

cues.visual: Dough has doubled in size, looks puffy

cook_steps.warnings: Rise time varies with room temperature - could be 45 min to 1.5 hours

cook_steps.instruction: About 30 minutes before dough is ready, preheat oven to 475°F. Place heavy baking sheet, cast iron pan, or baking tile on bottom shelf to preheat.

cues.visual: Oven is fully preheated, baking surface is screaming hot

cook_steps.warnings: The baking surface MUST be fully preheated for pitas to puff

cook_steps.instruction: Punch down risen dough. Divide into 8 equal pieces using bench scraper or knife. Form each piece into a small ball.

cues.audio: Satisfying thump when you punch down the dough

cook_steps.instruction: Place dough balls on work surface, cover with damp towel. Let rest 10 minutes.

cues.visual: Dough balls have relaxed and spread slightly

cook_steps.warnings: This rest makes rolling easier - don't skip it

cook_steps.instruction: Prepare a napkin-lined basket or bowl to hold finished pitas.

Take one dough ball (keep others covered). Press into a flat disk with your palm, then roll with rolling pin to 6-inch circle, then to 8-inch diameter, about 1/8 inch thick. Dust with flour as needed.

cues.visual: Thin, even circle - will shrink slightly when baked

cook_steps.warnings: Work quickly - dough dries out. If it springs back too much, let it rest another minute.

cook_steps.instruction: Carefully lift dough circle and place quickly on hot baking surface. Bake 2 minutes until puffed, then flip with tongs and bake 1 minute more.

cues.visual: Pita puffs dramatically into a balloon, surface has a few brown speckles but is mostly pale

cook_steps.warnings: The pita should be pale with only a few spots - don't over-brown

cook_steps.instruction: Transfer hot pita to napkin-lined basket, cover immediately to keep soft. Repeat rolling and baking with remaining dough balls.

cues.visual: All 8 pitas puffed and stacked in basket

cook_steps.warnings: Keep finished pitas covered so they stay soft

finishing.instructions: Serve warm. Pitas can be cut in half to form pockets for filling, or used whole for wrapping or dipping.
finishing.make_ahead: Dough can be refrigerated overnight after initial kneading - bring to room temperature before shaping. Baked pitas are best fresh.
finishing.storage: Store baked pitas in plastic bag at room temperature for 2 days. Freeze for up to 1 month. Reheat briefly in warm oven or toaster to refresh.

notes: The hot baking surface is the key to puffing - don't skip the preheat
Soft, moist dough makes tender pitas - resist over-flouring
If pitas don't puff: oven not hot enough, baking surface not hot enough, or dough rolled too thick
The sponge step develops flavor - don't skip the 15 minute wait
Rolling to 8 inches accounts for shrinkage during baking
